title: Prefixes (age 7+)
keyIdea: A prefix is a group of letters added to the front of a root word to change its meaning. dis- and un- mean not or the opposite (dislike, unfair), mis- means wrongly (misread), re- means again or back (replay), pre- means before (preheat), anti- means against (anticlockwise), auto- means self (autograph) and super- means above or more than (superstar). The root word keeps its spelling: write the whole prefix, then the whole root, so mis + spell = misspell and dis + appear = disappear. To check a word really has a prefix, take the letters off: a real word should be left (dish has no prefix, because h is not a word).
familyTip: Play prefix ping-pong: one person says a root word (like play, tidy or read), the other adds a prefix and says what the new word means. Then write the tricky ones together, such as misspell and disappear, and count the letters where the two parts meet.

visual.caption: What does the prefix mean? Drag each word, or tap it and then tap a box.

lab.caption: Flagship lab: clip on dis-, mis-, re- or pre- to fit a clue, spell misspell and disappear, sort by meaning, match anti-, auto- and super-, and spot fakes.

kid: A prefix is a small group of letters at the front of a word. It changes what the word means. The word it joins is the root word. Re + play is replay: play again.
Each prefix has a job. dis- and un- mean not: dislike, unfair. mis- means wrongly: misread. re- means again: redo. pre- means before: preheat.
Some prefixes are bigger. auto- means self: you write your autograph yourself. anti- means against: anticlockwise. super- means above or more: a superstar.

When you add a prefix, keep every letter. Mis and spell make misspell, with two s. Dis and appear make disappear, with one s. Some words just start with the same letters, like dish. Take dis off and h is not a word, so dish has no prefix.
adult: Ages 7 to 10. In England the Year 3 and 4 spelling appendix lists the prefixes un-, dis-, mis-, re-, sub-, inter-, super-, anti- and auto-, with the rule that most prefixes are added to the beginning of root words without any changes in spelling (examples: disappoint, misbehave, redo, superstar, antiseptic, autograph). Common Core L.3.4b and L.4.4b ask pupils to use a known affix as a clue to a word's meaning. This lesson adds pre-, which appears in the topic's list.

Meanings taught: dis- and un- mean not or the opposite of; mis- means wrongly or badly; re- means again or back; pre- means before; anti- means against; auto- means self or own; super- means above, over or more than. The spelling move is to write the whole prefix and then the whole root, which is why some words get a double letter at the join (misspell, dissatisfied) and others do not (disappear, mistake).

Common mistakes: dropping a letter at the join (mispell, disatisfied); adding one (dissappear, dissapoint); choosing a prefix with the wrong meaning (misagree for disagree); reading auto- as car because of 'autos'; and treating any word that starts with the same letters as prefixed (dish, ready, mister, reach). Teach the check: take the prefix off and see whether a real, related word is left.

practice.hint: Write all of mis, then all of spell.
practice.explain: Keep every letter: mis + spell = misspell, with two s where the parts meet.

practice.prompt: What does mis- mean in misbehave?
practice.explain: mis- means wrongly or badly, so misbehave means behave badly.

practice.prompt: A root word has {h} letters. You add the prefix mis- to the front. How many letters does the new word have?
practice.hint: mis adds three letters, and the root word keeps all of its letters.
practice.explain: The root keeps all {h} letters and mis adds 3, so the new word has {=h+3} letters.

practice.prompt: Sam reads a comic once. Then he rereads it {n} times. How many times has he read it in all?
practice.hint: re- means again, so each reread is one more read.
practice.explain: 1 first read and {n} rereads make {=n+1} reads in all.

practice.prompt: Which word does NOT have a prefix?
practice.hint: Take the first letters off. Is a real word left?
practice.explain: Take dis off dish and you get h, which is not a word. dislike and disobey leave like and obey.

pool.prompt: A word starts with the prefix dis- and has {h} letters in all. How many letters are in its root word?
pool.hint: Take the prefix off. dis has three letters.
pool.explain: {h} letters take away the 3 letters of dis leaves {=h-3} letters in the root word, which keeps its spelling.
pre- means before, so preheat means heat before. reheat means heat again.

pool.hint: dis ends in s. What does satisfied start with?
pool.explain: dis + satisfied keeps both s letters: dissatisfied. Nothing in the root changes.

choices: your own name, written by you
pool.hint: auto- means self or own, as in autopilot.
pool.explain: auto- means self, so an autograph is your name written by yourself. It has nothing to do with cars.

pool.prompt: Which word means 'against the way clock hands turn'?
pool.explain: anti- means against, so anticlockwise means turning against the clock hands.

pool.prompt: Which word has the prefix re-?
pool.hint: Take re off. Which leaves a real word?
pool.explain: re + write = rewrite, write again. Take re off ready or reach and no word is left.

choices: She added an s: appear does not start with s
pool.explain: dis + appear = disappear, with one s and two p. The extra s is not in either part.

pool.prompt: A root word has {h} letters. You add the prefix super- to the front. How many letters does the new word have?
pool.hint: Count the letters in super, then add the root word's letters.
pool.explain: super has 5 letters and the root keeps all {h}, so the new word has {=h+5} letters.
